slides.1.title: Moscatel de Setúbal in Depth: Roxo and Aged Versions
slides.1.html:
Moscatel de Setúbal DOC is one of Portugal's most famous sweet wines, known for its unique skin-contact method.

🌸 Two Varietal Versions

  • Moscatel de Setúbal (yellow): made from Muscat of Alexandria (= Moscatel Graúdo), the more common version, with orange blossom・apricot・honey
  • Moscatel Roxo (purple) ⭐: made from a rare purple variety, with rose・raspberry・violet; produced in tiny quantities and Portugal's rarest sweet wine

⏳ Evolution with Age

  • 5–10 years: deep gold, intense Muscat floral notes, orange blossom and apricot, silky and luscious
  • 20–30 years: deep amber, toffee, orange peel and nuts; still richly sweet but more complex
  • 50+ years: top old vintages from José Maria da Fonseca, very dark in colour, dense with coffee and caramel, still sweet, and astonishing

🔬 The Unique Skin Maceration Method

  • After fortification, fresh Moscatel grape skins are added to the wine and macerated for 3–6 months (other fortified wines have no such step)
  • This step greatly increases the intensity of the Muscat floral character and the silkiness of the palate
slides.2.title: Comparing Portugal's Sweet Wine Types
slides.2.items.0.desc: Muscat fortified + skin maceration, exceptional floral character, can age for 50–100 years, Setúbal Peninsula
slides.2.items.1.desc: Multi-variety blend fortified, fruity or oxidative, 20–50 years of ageing, Douro Valley
slides.2.items.2.desc: Heating and oxidation, the longest-lived, ageing for a century, Madeira island
slides.2.items.3.desc: Off-dry fortified wine, Lisbon outskirts, nearly extinct, produced only by Quinta dos Pesos, with nutty toffee notes
slides.3.question: What is the purpose of the step of "macerating fresh grape skins" in making Moscatel de Setúbal?
slides.3.options.0: To deepen the colour of the wine
slides.3.options.2: To greatly increase the intensity of the Muscat floral character, the biggest difference between Moscatel de Setúbal and other fortified sweet wines
slides.3.options.3: To lower acidity and make the palate rounder
slides.3.explanation: After fortification, Moscatel de Setúbal undergoes an additional 3–6 months of maceration on fresh grape skins. This unique step (absent from other fortified wines) lets the Moscatel's natural aromatic compounds (terpenes) dissolve into the wine in large quantities, making the Muscat and orange blossom aromas exceptionally intense, which is the core stylistic feature of Moscatel de Setúbal.
slides.4.question: "Moscatel Roxo" is the rarest sweet wine of which Portuguese region, and what colour is the grape variety?
slides.4.options.1: The Setúbal Peninsula, a purple Moscatel variety, with rose and raspberry aromas
slides.4.explanation: Moscatel Roxo (purple Moscatel) is the rarest sweet wine of the Setúbal Peninsula DOC. It is made from an extremely rare Muscat variety with purple skins, giving distinctive rose・raspberry・violet aromas. It is completely different from the ordinary golden Moscatel de Setúbal, produced in tiny quantities, and is one of Portugal's rarest sweet wines.
